At the finite-moment law delta_0, vanishing uniform perturbation directions that move tiny probability to a remote point give a nonzero mean difference quotient, so the mean fails Hadamard differentiability even on the finite-second-moment subdomain. Neither counterexample uses nonmeasurability or undefined moments. The norm, CDF and mean definitions have genuine values on these witnesses.

Negates integrated squared-risk convergence on an analytic-CEF compact-density subdomain. The canonical assertion says consistency across regions of nonzero probability mass and does not define it as integrated squared-risk convergence; that interpretation appears only in audit history. Failure of this interpretation alone cannot be labelled a refutation of the canonical assertion. The narrower analytic/density witness domain is legitimate for refuting an explicit L2 assertion, and finite second moments are usual BLP conditions. Missing explicit fit measurability is not used as a counterexample: eventually J<n and an iid continuous design is full rank almost surely, forcing any fit to agree almost surely with the unique measurable sample least-squares fit.
